contexts.text: It is a fallacy of the merely natural sense that there are simple substances, which are monads and atoms; for whatever is within the external Sensual, the natural man believes to be of such a character, or else nothing.

They who do not know these things, and who do not thus distinguish the objects of reason, cannot but terminate the ideas of their thought in either the atoms of Epicurus, the monads of Leibnitz, or the simple substances of Wolff, and so shut up their understanding as with a bolt...
